question.prompt: Suppose that the roots of the polynomial \(P(x) = x^3 + ax^2 + bx + c\) are \(\cos\tfrac{2\pi}{7},\) \(\cos\tfrac{4\pi}{7},\) and \(\cos\tfrac{6\pi}{7},\) where angles are in radians. What is \(abc?\)

solutions.title: Use cosine identities and Vieta
solutions.explanation:
The useful observation is that adding or doubling these angles produces the same three cosine values after angle reduction.

Write
\[
r=\cos\frac{2\pi}{7},\qquad s=\cos\frac{4\pi}{7},\qquad t=\cos\frac{6\pi}{7},
\]
and let \(S=r+s+t\) and \(T=rs+rt+st\). Vieta's formulas give
\[
a=-S,\qquad b=T,\qquad c=-rst.
\]
Adding the cosine addition and subtraction formulas gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\cos(A+B)+\cos(A-B)
&=(\cos A\cos B-\sin A\sin B)\\
&\quad+(\cos A\cos B+\sin A\sin B)\\
&=2\cos A\cos B.
\end{aligned}
\]
This product-to-sum identity, together with \(\cos(2\pi-\theta)=\cos\theta\), gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
2rs&=\cos\frac{6\pi}{7}+\cos\frac{2\pi}{7}=t+r,\\
2rt&=\cos\frac{8\pi}{7}+\cos\frac{4\pi}{7}=t+s,\\
2st&=\cos\frac{10\pi}{7}+\cos\frac{2\pi}{7}=s+r.
\end{aligned}
\]
Adding these equations shows that \(T=S\).

The double-angle formula also gives
\[
2r^2-1=s,\qquad 2s^2-1=t,\qquad 2t^2-1=r.
\]
Therefore
\[
S=2(r^2+s^2+t^2)-3
 =2(S^2-2T)-3
 =2S^2-4S-3.
\]
Thus
\[
2S^2-5S-3=(2S+1)(S-3)=0.
\]
Each of \(r,s,t\) is less than \(1\), so \(S<3\). Hence \(S=-\tfrac12\), which gives \(a=\tfrac12\) and \(b=-\tfrac12\).

Finally, using \(2rs=t+r\),
\[
4rst=2t(t+r)=2t^2+2rt
=(1+r)+(t+s)=1+S=\frac12.
\]
So \(rst=\tfrac18\) and \(c=-\tfrac18\). The requested product is
\[
abc=\frac12\left(-\frac12\right)\left(-\frac18\right)
=\boxed{\frac1{32}}.
\]
The answer is choice \(\text{D}\).
